reference.driver_not_used: pyuvsim.run_uvdata_uvsim requires mpi4py, which is not in the crossval feature; the engine it distributes tasks to is called directly instead

host.note: linux-64 and osx-64 were not exercised; the pixi lock resolves pyuvsim 1.4.0 on all three platforms but only osx-arm64 was run

setup.beam: one BeamFITS file, read by both codes, whose E-field response is exactly 1 over the whole visible hemisphere
setup.sky: one skyh5 file, read by both codes

convention_mappings: 1. Fringe sign: RadioSim exp(-2i*pi*(u*l+v*m+w*(n-1))), pyuvsim exp(+2i*pi*(u*l+v*m+w*n)); both use antenna2-antenna1 in ENU. With a coplanar array (w == 0) and identical per-antenna Jones matrices the two cubes are per-baseline Hermitian conjugates.
2. Coherency Stokes-V sign: RadioSim uses (1/2)[[I+Q, U+iV],[U-iV, I-Q]]; pyradiosky 1.1.0 uses 0.5*[[I+Q, U-iV],[U+iV, I-Q]].
3. Local polarization basis axis order: the two local receptor frames are each other's axis swap, which flips Stokes Q and Stokes V. Mappings 2 and 3 both flip V, so V agrees and Q does not.

cases.compares: the full (time, baseline, frequency, correlation) visibility cube for four unpolarized point sources, no jones: section, fixed mount, unit beam
cases.exercises: K (geometric phase), ENU baseline vectors, ICRS->AltAz, sidereal time, direction cosines, Jy-to-coherency normalisation

cases.compares: the local Stokes decomposition of the same cube for three full-Stokes point sources on an alt-az array with jones.P enabled
cases.exercises: everything above plus P (parallactic rotation) against pyradiosky's exact ICRS->AltAz coherency rotation
cases.verdict: total intensity and circular polarization agree to 2e-10 and 4e-11 relative; the polarized intensity is preserved (the fitted ratio modulus is 1 to 2e-5) and the linear polarization agrees to 2.1e-3 relative after the documented axis swap

unresolved.item: the sign of local Stokes Q
unresolved.detail: RadioSim's local Q has the opposite sign to pyuvsim's for the same sky, beam file and mount. Mapping 3 describes it as an axis-order convention, and the preserved polarized intensity is consistent with that, but this comparison does not establish which convention is the intended one for an east-oriented x feed.

After the axis swap the two local polarization frames still differ by a fitted -0.0576 degrees. An independent astropy probe at the same epoch and sources measures 0.200 degrees between the position angle of ICRS north and the apparent-equatorial parallactic angle, so a reference-frame difference of this species is present at the right order of magnitude, but the two numbers were not reconciled.
